ca_calawee_cliffs.blurb: Calawee Cliffs is a small lakeside crag on the west shore of Lake Tahoe, inside the state park at Bliss, where the walls drop almost straight into the water. All ten climbs are traditional leads, running from easy fifth class through the moderate 5.7 to 5.10 range, with a single route up at 5.12. Most have fixed chained anchors at the top, and a long rope is needed to get lowered from many of them; some lines can also be top-roped. The setting is the draw: a summer day here is shared with swimmers and boaters, so it can be lively and loud, and a few starts are only reachable by boat or paddleboard when the lake is high.

ca_c_castle_rock_southeast_face.blurb: The Southeast Face is a recessed section of Castle Rock in the San Bernardino Mountains above Big Bear Lake, tucked between the South Face and the Black Tower Buttress. Ten climbs here are mostly traditional leads, with two top-rope lines, and the grades stay friendly: nearly everything falls between 5.6 and 5.9, topped by one 5.10 classic. It is a good pick for climbers building up on gear who want a high-elevation, quiet crag. The hillside is steep and breezy, afternoons can turn chilly, and the crowds thicken in summer. Snow can sit on the trail in the colder months, so check conditions in spring.

ca_vasquez_rocks.blurb: Vasquez Rocks is a county park near Agua Dulce, between Santa Clarita and Palmdale, famous for huge slabs of rock tilted up out of the desert floor. The climbing is modest and mostly low-effort: six boulder problems, three top-rope lines and a lone trad route, with the problems running from very easy up to one hard outlier and the roped routes landing in the lower to middle 5th-class range. The rock is brittle, so expect to move carefully and test holds. It suits a casual outing, a short training session or a beginner, rather than a full day of climbing, and you can also wander the formations on foot.
